project.name: waggle-os
project.description: Waggle OS is a workspace-native AI agent platform with persistent memory, model-agnostic orchestration, and skill-extensible capabilities, delivered as a Tauri desktop app (React 19 + Vite) with a Fastify Node.js sidecar over an npm monorepo. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: validateInstance
nodes.summary: Validates a corpus instance against required fields and constraints, returning a list of constraint violations.

nodes.name: runSpotAudit
nodes.summary: Runs a spot audit over a sample of corpus instances, re-validating each and returning pass/fail results per instance.

nodes.name: fitness.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the GEPA fitness scoring functions including tiered fitness, retrieval engagement bonus, cost penalty, and delta-floor verdict for prompt shape candidates.

nodes.name: computeTieredFitness
nodes.summary: Computes the full tiered fitness score for a candidate by combining pass rate, retrieval engagement bonus, and cost penalty across two tiers.

nodes.name: computeDeltaFloorVerdict
nodes.summary: Computes a statistical delta-floor verdict comparing a candidate to the incumbent by binomial confidence interval analysis.

nodes.name: mutation-oracle-fork.ts
nodes.summary: Provides utilities for the GEPA mutation oracle fork: shape classification, template path resolution, template loading, and oracle prompt construction.

nodes.name: mutation-validator.ts
nodes.summary: Validates mutated prompt-shape candidate files by checking SHA-256 integrity, structural constraints, and that the MULTI_STEP_ACTION_CONTRACT bytes are preserved unchanged.

nodes.name: validateCandidate
nodes.summary: Validates a mutation candidate file: checks file existence, structural shape, and byte-level integrity of the immutable MULTI_STEP_ACTION_CONTRACT section.

nodes.name: selection.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the GEPA candidate selection algorithm: ranks evaluated candidates by fitness, applies acceptance gate, and selects the winning shape for promotion.

nodes.name: runSelection
nodes.summary: Runs the full selection pass over evaluated candidates, scoring each against the incumbent via acceptance criteria and returning the selected winner.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines all shared TypeScript types and interfaces for the GEPA faza-1 benchmark: corpus instances, candidates, fitness records, evaluation results, and acceptance outcomes.

nodes.name: acceptance.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest unit tests for the GEPA faza-1 acceptance module, covering threshold checks and edge cases for candidate evaluation.

nodes.name: corpus.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest unit tests for the GEPA corpus module, validating instance construction, stratification cells, and spot-audit utilities.

nodes.name: fitness.test.ts
nodes.summary: Comprehensive Vitest unit tests for the GEPA fitness scoring functions, covering all scoring tiers, bonuses, penalties, and statistical verdict calculations.

nodes.name: mutation-oracle-fork.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest unit tests for the mutation-oracle-fork utilities, validating shape classification, template resolution, and oracle prompt construction.

nodes.name: selection.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest unit tests for the GEPA selection algorithm, covering candidate ranking, acceptance gate behavior, and promotion logic.

nodes.name: cost-probe.ts
nodes.summary: Cost probing script for GEPA phase-5 evolved shapes, measuring token usage and latency distributions across Claude and Qwen evolved shape variants via LiteLLM.

nodes.name: callViaLitellm
nodes.summary: Makes a single LLM inference call via the LiteLLM proxy, recording token counts, cost, and latency.

nodes.name: probe
nodes.summary: Runs a series of LLM inference probes for a given prompt shape, collecting latency and cost samples for statistical analysis.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point: probes all registered evolved shapes, aggregates statistics, and prints a comparison report with percentile breakdowns.

nodes.name: behavioral-spec.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the canonical BEHAVIORAL_SPEC rules for the Waggle agent, organized into named sections with CRITICAL markers, and exports the active spec builder used by the system prompt loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports BEHAVIORAL_SPEC (static rules string), COMPACTION_PROMPT (static string), and buildActiveBehavioralSpec (function) — a deliberate split between static content and runtime assembly.

nodes.name: buildActiveBehavioralSpec
nodes.summary: Assembles the active behavioral spec string by merging base BEHAVIORAL_SPEC with any runtime overrides, enabling per-session customization without mutating the static spec.

nodes.name: phase-5-router.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the GEPA Phase-5 canary routing logic that deterministically assigns agent requests to evolved prompt-shape variants based on a hashed bucket percentage.

nodes.name: routeRequestToVariant
nodes.summary: Routes an incoming agent request to either the canary variant or the base shape based on the request's hash bucket and the configured canary percentage.

nodes.name: context-compressor.ts
nodes.summary: Provides conversation context compression utilities for the agent: token estimation, tool-result pruning, middle-section summarization, and a main compressConversation pipeline.

nodes.name: compressConversation
nodes.summary: Main pipeline: determines whether compression is needed, then prunes tool results and/or summarizes the middle portion of the conversation to fit within token budget.

nodes.name: summarizeMiddle
nodes.summary: Calls the LLM to summarize the middle (non-protected) segment of the conversation, replacing it with a compact summary message.

nodes.name: feature-flags.ts
nodes.summary: Defines and exports runtime feature flags for the agent package, including GEPA Phase-5 canary percentage parsing and per-flag enable/disable checks.

nodes.name: parsePhase5CanaryPct
nodes.summary: Parses the GEPA_PHASE5_CANARY_PCT environment variable, clamping the value to [0,100] with a safe default.

nodes.name: checkpoint.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the CheckpointStore class for persistent agent task checkpointing — saves and loads task state to/from disk between agent loop iterations for resumability.

nodes.name: CheckpointStore
nodes.summary: Manages the lifecycle of a long-task checkpoint directory, supporting save, load, integrity verification, and cleanup of step-based state snapshots.

nodes.name: context-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Implements ContextManager for long-running agent tasks, integrating context compression, retrieval-cache eviction, and decision-history summarization to maintain a healthy token budget across iterations.

nodes.name: ContextManager
nodes.summary: Orchestrates token-budget management for long agent tasks: compresses messages, evicts stale retrieval cache, and summarizes decision history when approaching context limits.

nodes.name: failure-classify.ts
nodes.summary: Implements a rule-cascade + LLM-judge failure classification system for agent task responses, categorizing failures into structured types (format violation, wrong entity, metadata copy, etc.) for benchmark analysis.

nodes.name: classifyFailure
nodes.summary: Top-level failure classifier: runs the rule cascade first, falls back to LLM judge when rules are inconclusive, and returns a typed FailureClassification.

nodes.name: classifyFailureBatch
nodes.summary: Classifies a batch of agent responses in parallel, returning an array of FailureClassification objects.

nodes.name: messages-compressor.ts
nodes.summary: Provides LLM-backed message array compression for long-task agent loops: estimates token count, splits into protected/compressible regions, and summarizes the middle via LLM call.

nodes.name: maybeCompressMessages
nodes.summary: Conditionally compresses the message array when token usage exceeds the threshold, replacing the middle segment with an LLM-generated summary.

nodes.name: recovery.ts
nodes.summary: Implements RecoveryRunner for long-task agent execution: wraps the agent loop with checkpoint-based retry, exponential backoff, and structured error/success state building.

nodes.name: RecoveryRunner
nodes.summary: Orchestrates long-task recovery by resolving starting checkpoints, executing the agent loop with retries, and persisting success/error state on completion.

nodes.name: report.ts
nodes.summary: Generates structured evaluation reports for long-task agent runs: computes cell metrics, builds cross-model accuracy matrices, identifies regressions, and renders markdown summaries.

nodes.name: generateReport
nodes.summary: Orchestrates full report generation from pilot records: computes all metrics, builds the matrix, identifies best models and regressions, and assembles a ReportOutput.

nodes.name: renderSummaryMd
nodes.summary: Renders a markdown summary report from computed metrics, including pass rates, confidence intervals, failure distributions, and regression notes.

nodes.name: output-normalize.ts
nodes.summary: Normalizes raw LLM output text for benchmark evaluation by applying configurable transformation passes: stripping think tags, answer labels, markdown fences, copied metadata, and collapsing blank lines.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Applies a sequence of configured normalization passes to LLM output text, returning the cleaned string for downstream evaluation.

nodes.name: claude.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the default Claude-targeted prompt shape, embedding the MULTI_STEP_ACTION_CONTRACT and registering it with the shape registry on module load.

nodes.name: generic-simple.ts
nodes.summary: Defines a generic, model-agnostic simple prompt shape without chain-of-thought scaffolding, registering it with the shape registry for use in non-Claude model contexts.

nodes.name: claude-gen1-v1.ts
nodes.summary: First-generation GEPA-evolved prompt shape for Claude models (v1), implementing structured XML-tagged reasoning protocols with explicit sub-question decomposition and grounding rules for the retrieval agent loop.

nodes.name: claude-gen1-v2.ts
nodes.summary: Second iteration of the GEPA-evolved Claude prompt shape (v2), refining retrieval engagement prompts with explicit multi-retrieval guidance and reasoning scaffold for improved coverage on multi-faceted questions.

nodes.name: generic-simple-gen1-v1.ts
nodes.summary: GEPA-evolved generic simple prompt shape (gen1/v1) targeting model-agnostic retrieval agents with a concise planning scaffold emphasizing multi-retrieval coverage and grounding discipline.

nodes.name: generic-simple-gen1-v2.ts
nodes.summary: Compact GEPA-evolved generic simple prompt shape (gen1/v2) with terse instruction style, per-turn reasoning loop, and iterative retrieval gap-filling procedure for budget-constrained runs.

nodes.name: gpt-gen1-v1.ts
nodes.summary: GEPA-evolved GPT prompt shape (gen1/v1) with compact inline instruction style, emphasizing gap-driven retrieval planning and multi-coverage before finalization.

nodes.name: gpt-gen1-v2.ts
nodes.summary: Second GEPA-evolved GPT prompt shape (gen1/v2), extending v1 with per-turn facet reasoning protocol and explicit counter-evidence probing to reduce hallucinated specifics.

nodes.name: qwen-non-thinking-gen1-v1.ts
nodes.summary: GEPA-evolved prompt shape for Qwen non-thinking mode (gen1/v1), using JSON-only output protocol and enforcing at-least-two-retrieval discipline before finalization.

nodes.name: qwen-non-thinking-gen1-v2.ts
nodes.summary: Refined GEPA-evolved Qwen non-thinking shape (gen1/v2), adding a kickoff prompt that primes broad-then-targeted retrieval and an iterative gap-check prompt after each retrieval result.

nodes.name: qwen-thinking-gen1-v1.ts
nodes.summary: GEPA-evolved prompt shape for Qwen thinking-mode models (gen1/v1), leveraging extended reasoning with markdown-structured headers and explicit retrieval discipline requiring at least two distinct queries.

nodes.name: qwen-thinking-gen1-v2.ts
nodes.summary: Compact GEPA-evolved Qwen thinking shape (gen1/v2) with tightened finalization gate: requires 2-3 distinct retrievals, explicit sub-part gap tracking, and conflict-of-distinct-risks check before finalizing.

nodes.name: gpt.ts
nodes.summary: Baseline GPT prompt shape implementing the PromptShape interface with minimal, concrete instructions for solo and multi-step retrieval agent modes.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Public barrel for the prompt-shapes module, re-exporting all shape implementations (claude, qwen-thinking, qwen-non-thinking, gpt, generic-simple, gepa-evolved variants), types, and the selector API.

nodes.name: qwen-non-thinking.ts
nodes.summary: Baseline prompt shape for Qwen non-thinking models with JSON-only output constraint, straightforward retrieval protocol, and minimal instruction overhead for budget-sensitive runs.

nodes.name: qwen-thinking.ts
nodes.summary: Baseline prompt shape for Qwen extended-thinking models, using markdown-structured headers to scaffold retrieval protocol and system/user/kickoff/injection message templates.

nodes.name: selector.ts
nodes.summary: Dynamic prompt shape selector with a runtime registry supporting exact-match and prefix-pattern routing; reads optional JSON config to override shape assignments per model alias without code changes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a module-level REGISTRY map and optional JSON config file loaded at runtime with a cache-reset escape hatch (_resetConfigCache) for testing.

nodes.name: selectShape
nodes.summary: Resolves a PromptShape for a given model alias by consulting exact-match and prefix-pattern overrides from a JSON config, falling back to the REGISTRY default.

nodes.name: registerShape
nodes.summary: Registers a named PromptShape into the module-level REGISTRY, throwing if the name is already taken to prevent silent overrides.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Core TypeScript type definitions for the prompt-shapes module — PromptShape interface, input types for solo/multi-step/retrieval-injection messages, and the MULTI_STEP_ACTION_CONTRACT constant string.

nodes.name: retrieval-agent-loop.ts
nodes.summary: Core retrieval agent execution engine implementing solo-run, multi-step retrieval loop, and recovery-wrapped variants; orchestrates LLM calls, prompt shape selection, context compression, checkpointing, and prediction capture.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest file in the agent package (973 lines); three exported entry points cover progressive complexity: solo → multi-step loop → loop with exponential-backoff recovery.

nodes.name: runRetrievalAgentLoop
nodes.summary: Main multi-turn retrieval agent loop: drives LLM inference, parses retrieve/finalize actions, injects search results, manages context compression and checkpointing across up to maxSteps turns.

nodes.name: runSoloAgent
nodes.summary: Single-turn agent variant that assembles a solo user prompt from pre-retrieved materials and calls the LLM once without a retrieval loop, useful for direct-context evaluation.

nodes.name: runRetrievalAgentLoopWithRecovery
nodes.summary: Wraps runRetrievalAgentLoop with configurable retry count and exponential backoff, enabling resilient batch evaluation runs that survive transient LLM provider errors.

nodes.name: applyContextCompression
nodes.summary: Checks whether message history exceeds the context budget and invokes the ContextManager to compress, emitting a compression event for observability.

nodes.name: recordPredictionIfCapturing
nodes.summary: Conditionally records a prediction into the RunMetaCapture object when capture mode is active, including cost, tokens, and turn-level audit trail.

nodes.name: run-meta.ts
nodes.summary: Provides RunMetaCapture for collecting per-run evaluation metadata (predictions, judge calls, model versions, cost) and RunMetaReader for loading serialized run artifacts including gzip-compressed raw responses.

nodes.name: RunMetaCapture
nodes.summary: Mutable accumulator for a single evaluation run's metadata — records predictions, judge call traces, model versions, and provider routes, then serializes to a JSONL + gzip artifact pair on disk.

nodes.name: RunMetaReader
nodes.summary: Reads serialized run metadata artifacts from disk, lazy-loading gzip-compressed raw LLM responses on demand via loadRawResponse.

nodes.name: verifyDeterministicReplay
nodes.summary: Replays a completed run through a provided function and asserts that every prediction output matches the stored value, surfacing any non-determinism in the evaluation pipeline.

nodes.name: behavioral-spec-overrides.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the behavioral spec override mechanism, verifying that buildActiveBehavioralSpec correctly merges rule overrides and that COMPACTION_PROMPT is well-formed.

nodes.name: context-compressor.test.ts
nodes.summary: Comprehensive Vitest tests for the context compression subsystem, covering token estimation, pruning, protected-region splitting, middle summarization, and full compression pipeline with mocked LLM calls.

nodes.name: feature-flags.test.ts
nodes.summary: Small Vitest suite testing FEATURE_FLAGS parsing and the isEnabled/parsePhase5CanaryPct helpers for environment-driven feature flag resolution.

nodes.name: long-task-checkpoint.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the long-task CheckpointStore and state-transition logic, covering schema versioning, save/load round-trips, makeInitialState, and nextStateFrom transitions.

nodes.name: long-task-context-manager.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for ContextManager integration with the retrieval agent loop, verifying token estimation, compression thresholds, cache eviction, and turn-level event emission.

nodes.name: long-task-failure-classify.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the failure classification subsystem, validating classifyFailure/classifyFailureBatch categorize agent errors (timeout, budget, parse, tool) and failureDistribution aggregates correctly.

nodes.name: long-task-loop-integration.test.ts
nodes.summary: End-to-end integration Vitest tests for the retrieval agent loop with scripted LLM responses, verifying checkpoint persistence, message compression triggers, and multi-turn flow control.

nodes.name: long-task-messages-compressor.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the message compression subsystem, testing shouldCompressMessages thresholds and maybeCompressMessages behavior under scripted LLM summarization calls within the loop context.

nodes.name: long-task-recovery.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the RecoveryRunner, simulating flaky step functions to verify retry logic, backoff timing, checkpoint-based resume, and deterministic-replay guarantees.

nodes.name: long-task-report.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for long-task report generation, validating generateReport, writeReportToDisk, and fromPilotRecord over synthetic pilot records with controlled outcome distributions.

nodes.name: output-normalize.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the output normalization pipeline, exercising normalize/normalizeWithPreset across multiple PRESETS to verify whitespace, JSON extraction, and answer-extraction behavior.

nodes.name: phase-5-canary-router.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the Phase 5 canary routing system, validating hashRequestIdToBucket distribution, routeRequestToVariant assignment, and BASE_TO_CANARY_VARIANT_MAP consistency with registered shapes.

nodes.name: prompt-shapes.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the prompt shapes module, verifying selectShape resolution, REGISTRY completeness, and that each registered shape produces valid system/user/injection prompts for representative inputs.

nodes.name: retrieval-agent-loop.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for the retrieval agent loop and run meta integration, using scripted LLM replies and mock search to verify multi-turn action parsing, prediction recording, and result structure.

nodes.name: run-meta.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest tests for RunMetaCapture and RunMetaReader, verifying serialization round-trips, gzip compression of raw responses, prediction indexing, and deterministic-replay validation.

nodes.name: chatgpt-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the ChatGPTAdapter class that parses ChatGPT conversation export JSON files into the hive-mind harvest item format, handling multiple conversation structures and tree-based message mappings.

nodes.name: ChatGPTAdapter
nodes.summary: Parses ChatGPT export JSON into normalized harvest items, traversing mapping trees and extracting text from multi-part message content.

nodes.name: chunk-utils.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a paragraph-based text chunking utility used by PDF and plaintext adapters to split large documents into manageable segments.

nodes.name: chunkByParagraphs
nodes.summary: Splits text into chunks at paragraph boundaries, respecting a maximum length constraint.

nodes.name: claude-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the ClaudeAdapter class that parses Claude.ai export JSON, handling conversations, project docs, memories, and design chat records into normalized harvest items.

nodes.name: ClaudeAdapter
nodes.summary: Multi-format Claude export parser supporting conversations, project docs, memories, and design chats with structured content block handling.

nodes.name: claude-code-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the ClaudeCodeAdapter class that scans local Claude Code project directories, extracting memory files, plans, preferences, and decision records into harvest items.

nodes.name: ClaudeCodeAdapter
nodes.summary: Scans Claude Code project directories for memory docs, plans, preferences, and mind-dir files, extracting structured decision records via pattern matching.

nodes.name: dedup.ts
nodes.summary: Provides content deduplication for harvest items using SHA-256 content hashes and trigram similarity scoring to filter out near-duplicate entries.

nodes.name: dedup
nodes.summary: Filters incoming harvest items against existing content using hash-exact and trigram-similarity deduplication, returning unique items and flagged contradictions.

nodes.name: harvestSetHash
nodes.summary: Computes a stable SHA-256 hash over a sorted set of harvest items for idempotent run detection.

nodes.name: extract-kg-entities.ts
nodes.summary: Extracts knowledge-graph entities from memory frames using LLM batch calls, writing named entities with types and properties into the KnowledgeGraph store with injection-scan protection.

nodes.name: extractKgEntities
nodes.summary: Batches dated frames, calls the LLM for entity extraction, and parses JSONL output into typed entity lists with error collection.

nodes.name: writeKgEntities
nodes.summary: Writes extracted entities to the KnowledgeGraph, merging with existing entities by name or creating new ones, with noise-name filtering.

nodes.name: extract-memory-lanes.ts
nodes.summary: Extracts facts, events, and profile cards from conversation text via three parallel LLM passes, writing them as typed memory frames with injection-scan protection.

nodes.name: extractMemoryLanes
nodes.summary: Runs three concurrent LLM extraction passes (facts, events, profiles) over a text input and collects results into typed lane arrays.

nodes.name: writeMemoryLaneFrames
nodes.summary: Writes fact, event, and profile extraction results as typed IFrames into the FrameStore, using injection-scan guards before each write.

nodes.name: gemini-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the GeminiAdapter class that parses Google Gemini/AI Studio export JSON into normalized harvest items, handling both array and nested conversation formats with media caption parity.

nodes.name: GeminiAdapter
nodes.summary: Parses Gemini export data supporting multiple conversation container shapes with W4.4 media-caption extraction for fileData and inlineData parts.

nodes.name: markdown-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the MarkdownAdapter that ingests markdown files or text, splitting by headings into section-level harvest items with bold-term tag extraction.

nodes.name: MarkdownAdapter
nodes.summary: Reads markdown from file paths or raw text, splits by heading-anchored sections, and extracts bold terms as metadata tags for each item.

nodes.name: pdf-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the PdfAdapter that dynamically imports pdf-parse to extract text from PDF files, splitting content into paragraph chunks for harvest ingestion.

nodes.name: PdfAdapter
nodes.summary: Uses dynamic import of pdf-parse to convert PDF buffers into chunked text harvest items with document metadata extracted from PDF info.

nodes.name: perplexity-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the PerplexityAdapter that parses Perplexity AI export formats (arrays, threads, single conversations) into harvest items with source-URL extraction.

nodes.name: PerplexityAdapter
nodes.summary: Handles multiple Perplexity export container shapes, extracts cited URLs as sources, and resolves ambiguous role labels across format variants.

nodes.name: pipeline.ts
nodes.summary: Core harvest processing pipeline implementing classify, extract, and synthesize stages with batched LLM calls, concurrency control, injection scanning, and deduplication.

nodes.name: HarvestPipeline
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full harvest pipeline: injection scan → classify → extract → synthesize → dedup, with configurable batch sizes, concurrency limits, and progress callbacks.

nodes.name: plaintext-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the PlaintextAdapter that reads plain text files or raw text input and chunks them into paragraph-based harvest items.

nodes.name: PlaintextAdapter
nodes.summary: Simple text ingestion adapter that reads files or raw strings and splits content into paragraph chunks for harvest processing.

nodes.name: prompts.ts
nodes.summary: Exports the three LLM prompt templates (CLASSIFY_PROMPT, EXTRACT_PROMPT, SYNTHESIZE_PROMPT) used by the harvest pipeline stages.

nodes.name: raw-turns.ts
nodes.summary: Manages raw conversation turn storage as IFrames in the FrameStore, providing header encoding/parsing utilities and the writeRawTurnFrames function for the raw-detail memory lane.

nodes.name: writeRawTurnFrames
nodes.summary: Writes individual conversation turn frames into the FrameStore with injection scan protection, per-turn deduplication by conversation key, and turn-count limiting.

nodes.name: raw-types.ts
nodes.summary: Provides type-safe runtime accessor utilities (asRecord, getString, getNumber, getArray, firstString) for safely traversing unknown JSON payloads from AI export files.

nodes.name: run-store.ts
nodes.summary: Implements HarvestRunStore, a SQLite-backed store for tracking harvest run lifecycle (start/heartbeat/complete/fail/abandon) with resumable interrupted-run detection.

nodes.name: HarvestRunStore
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed run tracker for harvest operations with status lifecycle management, progress heartbeat, and interrupted-run resumption queries.

nodes.name: source-store.ts
nodes.summary: Implements HarvestSourceStore, a SQLite-backed registry for harvest source configurations with auto-sync scheduling and stale-source detection.

nodes.name: HarvestSourceStore
nodes.summary: SQLite registry for harvest sources tracking display names, paths, sync counters, frame counts, and auto-sync intervals with stale-source queries.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the core harvest domain types and interfaces (HarvestItem, HarvestAdapter, HarvestSource, etc.) shared across all adapters and pipeline components.

nodes.name: universal-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the UniversalAdapter as a fallback parser that auto-detects source type by heuristic and handles arbitrary JSON conversation structures and plain-text formats.

nodes.name: UniversalAdapter
nodes.summary: Generic fallback adapter with source-type auto-detection, recursive conversation-tree discovery, and multi-format text/JSON parsing for unknown AI export shapes.

nodes.name: url-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the UrlAdapter that fetches web pages or parses inline HTML, extracting title, description, and section-split plain-text content as harvest items.

nodes.name: UrlAdapter
nodes.summary: Fetches URLs with timeout and parses HTML into structured harvest items using stripped plain text with heading-based sectioning.

nodes.name: injection-scanner.ts
nodes.summary: Exports scanForInjection(), a three-pattern security scanner that detects prompt-injection attempts in external content before it enters the memory substrate.

nodes.name: scanForInjection
nodes.summary: Tests text against three regex pattern sets (role override, instruction injection, context manipulation) and returns a scan result with matched flags and risk score.

nodes.name: logger.ts
nodes.summary: Exports createCoreLogger(), a lightweight tagged logger factory providing warn/info/error/fatal methods used throughout the hive-mind-core package.

nodes.name: createCoreLogger
nodes.summary: Factory that creates a tagged logger object routing warn/info/error/fatal to console methods, used as the package-wide logging abstraction.

nodes.name: api-embedder.ts
nodes.summary: Implements createApiEmbedder(), an HTTP-based embedding provider that calls an OpenAI-compatible embeddings API with timeout, batching, and dimension normalization.

nodes.name: createApiEmbedder
nodes.summary: Factory that creates an embedding client calling an HTTP API endpoint, with per-request timeout, dimension normalization, and both single-text and batch modes.

nodes.name: awareness.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the AwarenessLayer class providing SQLite-backed active-task and state tracking with priority ordering, TTL expiry, category filtering, and context serialization.

nodes.name: AwarenessLayer
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed awareness store tracking active tasks and state items with priority ordering, TTL expiry, category bucketing, metadata JSON fields, and context-string serialization.

nodes.name: chunker.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the mind chunker that splits memory frames into overlapping token-bounded segments for vector-indexed chunk retrieval (HybridSearch chunk lane).

nodes.name: concept-tracker.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the ConceptTracker class that maintains a SQLite-backed frequency map of concepts mentioned in memory frames, used for ontology and relevance scoring.

nodes.name: content-hash.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a SHA-256 content hashing utility for deduplicating memory frames at the storage layer, used by FrameStore and db.ts.

nodes.name: db.ts
nodes.summary: Central database initialization module that opens/creates the SQLite database, applies schema migrations, and provides the MindDb accessor class used by all mind subsystems.

nodes.name: embedding-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the EmbeddingProvider orchestrator that selects and initializes the appropriate embedder backend (in-process, API, LiteLLM, Ollama) based on configuration, with fallback logic and dimension validation.

nodes.name: embeddings.ts
nodes.summary: Re-exports the Embedder interface and related types as a barrel entry point for the embedding subsystem.

nodes.name: entity-normalizer.ts
nodes.summary: Provides entity name normalization and noise-name filtering utilities used during knowledge graph entity extraction to canonicalize names and filter out non-entity strings.

nodes.name: evolution-runs.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the EvolutionRunStore class for persisting and managing AI self-improvement evolution run records in SQLite, including lifecycle transitions (propose, accept, reject, deploy, fail) with status tracking and querying.

nodes.name: EvolutionRunStore
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed store for evolution run records that manages full lifecycle (proposed → accepted/rejected → deployed/failed) with UUID-keyed lookups, filtered listing, and status count aggregation.

nodes.name: execution-traces.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the ExecutionTraceStore class for recording, appending to, and querying agent execution traces stored in SQLite, capturing session context, cost, duration, and outcome for each agent invocation.

nodes.name: ExecutionTraceStore
nodes.summary: Manages execution trace records in SQLite, supporting start/append/finalize lifecycle, correction marking, filtered querying, and outcome count aggregation per persona/workspace/model.

nodes.name: frames.ts
nodes.summary: Core memory frame storage layer providing the FrameStore class that implements I/P/B-frame video-codec-inspired memory compression, FTS indexing, deduplication via content hashing, and compaction of older memory groups.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a video codec (I/P/B-frame) metaphor for memory compression: I-frames are full snapshots, P-frames are incremental patches, and B-frames are bidirectional references.

nodes.name: FrameStore
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed memory frame store implementing I/P/B-frame creation, GOP (group of pictures) reconstruction, FTS indexing, content-hash deduplication, access tracking, importance-based compaction, and vector index maintenance.

nodes.name: identity.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the IdentityLayer class for persisting and retrieving a single personal identity record (name, role, department, personality, capabilities) that can be injected into agent system prompts.

nodes.name: IdentityLayer
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed singleton identity store that creates, reads, and partially updates the user's personal identity record, with a toContext helper for agent prompt injection.

nodes.name: improvement-signals.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the ImprovementSignalStore class for tracking recurring agent behavior patterns (correction, confusion, tool failures) with frequency counters and actionable signal surfacing for the evolution subsystem.

nodes.name: ImprovementSignalStore
nodes.summary: Persists improvement signal patterns with upsert-on-conflict frequency counting, category-based retrieval, and actionable threshold filtering to surface the most impactful patterns for evolution.

nodes.name: inprocess-embedder.ts

tour.title: What Is Waggle OS?
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the product: a workspace-native AI agent platform whose distinguishing feature is persistent memory. This document lays out the architecture, the quick-start setup, and the environment variables, giving you the mental model of a memory-first AI workspace before you read a single line of code. Keep its 'memory is the moat' framing in mind — it explains why so much of the codebase orbits the substrate you will reach in Step 7.

tour.title: Frontend Entry Point
tour.description: This is where the running product actually begins. main.tsx is the React entry point that applies the stored theme before first paint (to avoid a flash of unstyled content), initializes analytics, and mounts the root App component, which in turn composes the full provider hierarchy: theme, Clerk auth, services, and install state, wrapped around the router. Following the import graph forward from here is the natural reading order for the entire UI.
tour.languageLesson: React apps bootstrap by calling createRoot(...).render(<App/>). The provider 'hierarchy' in App.tsx is the idiomatic way to make cross-cutting concerns (auth, theme, data clients) available to the whole tree via Context, instead of threading props down manually.

tour.title: The Desktop Cockpit Shell
tour.description: One level deeper from App lies the AppShell — the top-level 'OS' surface that orchestrates the boot sequence, workspace state, keyboard shortcuts, the dock, overlay visibility, and the layout of Sidebar, StatusBar, and ChatHost. This is the component that makes Waggle feel like a desktop operating system rather than a web page. Everything the user interacts with hangs off this shell, so it is the hub of the frontend dependency graph (high fan-out).

tour.title: How the UI Talks to the Backend
tour.description: The frontend never calls the server directly — every request flows through the LocalAdapter, the single most depended-upon file in the UI (highest fan-in in the whole frontend). It wraps each sidecar API call, manages the connection lifecycle with session-token refresh and 401-retry, and exposes SSE subscriptions, all behind one shared singleton. The ServiceProvider wires that adapter into React context so any component can read connection state. Understanding this boundary is the key to understanding how the cockpit from Step 3 stays in sync with the server you meet next.
tour.languageLesson: A singleton adapter behind a Context provider is a common pattern for centralizing all network I/O: retries, auth refresh, and streaming (SSE) live in one place, so call sites stay declarative and the cross-cutting connection logic is never duplicated.

tour.title: The Server: Fastify Sidecar
tour.description: On the other side of the adapter is the local sidecar — a Fastify server factory that registers roughly 80 route plugins and decorates the server with memory, vault, connectors, and scheduling infrastructure, seeding initial data on first run. This file is the backend's nerve center: it has the highest fan-out of any node in the project, because nearly every feature plugs a route into it. The adapter from Step 4 is calling exactly these routes.

tour.title: The Chat Pipeline — Where It All Connects
tour.description: Of the sidecar's many routes, the chat route is the spine of the product. It implements the full agent conversation pipeline: assembling the system prompt, scanning input for prompt injection, streaming the LLM response, executing tool calls, integrating memory, and delivering everything back over SSE. This single route ties together the agent runtime (Step 6's neighbor) and the memory substrate (Step 7), so it is the best vantage point for seeing how a user message becomes an agent action with memory recall.

tour.title: Agent Runtime: Loop, Orchestrator, Personas
tour.description: When the chat route runs an agent, it drives this subsystem. The agent-loop executes multi-turn LLM interactions, dispatching tool calls with retry logic, a loop guard, and completion gates. The orchestrator owns the memory substrate and builds each system prompt with persona and recalled-memory context, while the 17 built-in personas (pure data in persona-data, logic in personas) shape how each agent behaves. Together they turn the raw LLM into a memory-aware, role-specialized worker.
tour.languageLesson: Splitting personas into a pure-data module (persona-data.ts) and a logic module (personas.ts) is a deliberate separation of concerns: the declarative array is easy to extend and test, while behavior (lookup, prompt composition, custom-persona loading) stays isolated and side-effect-aware.

tour.title: Agent Tools — The Bridge to Memory
tour.description: Agents act through tools, and the mind-tool factory is where the runtime meets the moat. It creates save_memory, search_memory, list_memories, get_entity, add_awareness, and feedback tools, each wired directly to the memory substrate (HybridSearch, KnowledgeGraph, IdentityLayer, the Cognify pipeline). This is the concrete handoff from 'agent' to 'memory': when an agent remembers or recalls, it is calling these tools, which is why this file ranks near the top of fan-in across the whole codebase.

tour.title: The Memory Substrate — The Moat
tour.description: This is the heart of Waggle's strategy: persistent memory that is free forever to create lock-in. db.ts opens the SQLite database and applies migrations; FrameStore implements video-codec-inspired I/P/B-frame memory compression with FTS indexing and dedup; HybridSearch fuses FTS5 keyword search, ANN vector search, RRF, and optional cross-encoder reranking; the KnowledgeGraph stores entity-relations with temporal validity; and the IdentityLayer persists who the user is. The tools from Step 8 are thin wrappers over exactly these classes.

tour.title: Filling the Substrate: Harvest Ingestion
tour.description: Memory does not only accumulate from live chats — the harvest pipeline imports existing conversations and files (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini exports, PDFs, URLs) into the substrate you just toured. It runs a classify → extract → synthesize flow with batched LLM calls, concurrency control, injection scanning, and deduplication, producing the memory frames that FrameStore (Step 9) stores. This is how a brand-new install becomes immediately useful: it harvests a user's history into the moat.

tour.title: The Shared Data Model & Database Schema
tour.description: Beneath both UI and server sits a shared vocabulary. The shared types module declares 30+ canonical interfaces (User, Team, AgentDef, Task, WaggleMessage, Memory, Artifact, Connector) used across every package, and tiers.ts encodes the 5-tier subscription system (TRIAL/FREE/PRO/TEAMS/ENTERPRISE) that gates features everywhere. The Drizzle schema and the generated SQL migration turn those types into the actual relational tables — agents, tasks, and team_entities (note the temporal validity windows that mirror the KnowledgeGraph from Step 9).
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle ORM defines tables as TypeScript objects and generates SQL migrations from them, so the database schema and the application's types stay in lockstep — a single source of truth instead of hand-maintained SQL drifting from the code.

tour.title: Supporting Systems & How It Ships
tour.description: Finally, the systems around the core and how it reaches users. Evolution (EvolutionOrchestrator + IterativeGEPA) is a self-improvement loop that mutates and re-scores prompts behind quality gates; WaggleDance dispatches messages between agents for multi-agent coordination. To ship, the Tauri Rust shell registers IPC commands and the system tray, the Node sidecar runs as a bundled child process speaking over IPC, the three-stage Dockerfile produces a minimal Alpine image for the Teams server, docker-compose wires the local infra (Postgres, Redis, MinIO, LiteLLM), and the CI pipeline gates every push with type-checks, lint, unit, and E2E tests.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds (builder → native-builder → runtime) compile everything in fat intermediate stages but copy only the runtime artifacts into the final image, keeping the production image small while still rebuilding native modules like better-sqlite3 against the runtime's libc.
